policy_title: Transfer Work Visas and Overseas Student Policy from Home Office
stated: Transfer policy-making over work visas and overseas students out of the Home Office and into other departments. Replace the Conservatives’ arbitrary salary threshold with a more flexible merit-based system for work visas, with the relevant department working with employers in each sector to address specific needs. Exempt NHS and care staff from the £1,000-a-year Immigration Skills Charge, and reverse the Conservatives’ ban on care workers bringing partners and children.

source.quote: Transfer policy-making over work visas and overseas students out of the Home Office and into other departments. Replace the Conservatives’ arbitrary salary threshold with a more flexible merit-based system for work visas, with the relevant department working with employers in each sector to address specific needs as part of a long-term workforce strategy that also focuses on education and training to address skills gaps from within the UK. Exempt NHS and care staff from the £1,000-a-year Immigration Skills Charge, and reverse the Conservatives’ ban on care workers bringing partners and children.

bearing_set.reason: Exempting NHS and care staff from the £1,000/year Immigration Skills Charge and reversing the ban on care workers bringing family directly targets healthcare and care staffing capacity, a key driver of NHS waiting lists and service access.

The care-worker specific provisions (Skills Charge exemption, family reunion reversal) affect the supply of social care workers, directly bearing on social care access and cost for older people — a core O8 indicator.

Replacing the salary threshold with a sector-by-sector merit-based system is a broad labour market intervention whose effect on wage levels and job quality for UK workers in affected sectors is contested but non-negligible.

Reversing the ban on care workers bringing partners and children directly engages the civil right to family life (ECHR Art. 8) and equal treatment for a predominantly migrant worker category, placing it within O9's strict scope of civil liberties and equal treatment.

Shifting to a sector-specific, employer-informed merit-based system for work visas — rather than a single salary threshold — plausibly improves labour-market matching across the economy, with a real (if contested) effect on productivity and business investment.

membership_note: Four fundamentals earn real verdicts: improved NHS/care staffing (O3), improved social care supply for older people (O8), a contested wage-floor effect on domestic workers (O4), and aggregate labour-market matching (O13). Administrative transfer between departments is machinery-of-government and earns no separate verdict.
